title: Representative-normalized algebraic-space derived pullback tensor comparison
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $a:X\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use the actual adjunction-unit local tensor sections [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], their small-model transport and unbounded derived pullback with its shared counit and normalized K-flat tensor representative comparisons [def-sfb-space-derived-pullback-models], and pointed affine etale neighbourhoods [def-sfb-space-geometric-stalk-models]. The ordinary pullback tensor isomorphism is the unique map sending every local $b\otimes(m\otimes n)$ to $(b\otimes m)\otimes(1\otimes n)$, with pure sheaf tensors defined by the existing sheafification-unit construction [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison]. Its total-complex isomorphism is uniquely specified by this ordinary comparison on every summand $p+q=i$, preserving order and the differential $d\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d$. Define the canonical derived comparison as the unique natural isomorphism $La^*(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)\cong La^*E\otimes^{\mathbf L}La^*K$ whose value on every pair of flat-term K-flat representatives satisfies the square with this total comparison, the shared derived counits, and the specified derived tensor representative isomorphisms. The pullbacks of these representatives are again flat-term K-flat. The normalized ordinary and derived comparisons exist uniquely; definitions select only from these uniqueness specifications, not a bare existence of a tensor isomorphism.
